senses.en: an introduction to a speech, document, or law

ex.en: The preamble to the Constitution begins with "We the People."
ex.zh: 美國憲法的序言以「我們人民」開頭。

root.note: 走在前面的部分 → 序言

senses.en: not securely held; likely to fall or collapse
dependent on chance; uncertain and risky

ex.en: The climber found herself in a precarious position on the icy ledge.
ex.zh: 那位登山者發現自己在結冰的岩架上處境危險。

root.note: 要靠祈求別人才得到的 → 不穩的、靠不住的

senses.en: an action taken in advance to prevent something bad from happening

ex.en: As a precaution, please back up your files before the update.
ex.zh: 為了預防起見，更新前請先備份你的檔案。

root.note: 事先小心 → 預防措施

senses.en: to come before something in time, order, or position

ex.en: A short speech will precede the awards ceremony.
ex.zh: 頒獎典禮之前會有一段簡短的致詞。

root.note: 走在前面 → 先於

mn: precede 是「在前面」，proceed 是「繼續進行」，別搞混。

senses.en: the condition of being more important or coming first

ex.en: Safety must take precedence over speed on the construction site.
ex.zh: 在工地上，安全必須優先於速度。

root.note: 走在前面的地位 → 優先

mn: 常見片語 take precedence over：比…優先。

senses.en: an earlier event or decision used as an example or guide

ex.en: The court's ruling set a precedent for future privacy cases.
ex.zh: 法院的判決為日後的隱私權案件立下先例。

root.note: 之前發生過的事 → 先例

senses.en: serving as or relating to a precedent

ex.en: The appeals court said its decision had no precedential value.
ex.zh: 上訴法院表示其判決不具先例效力。

root.note: 先例的

senses.en: the slow change in the direction of the axis of a spinning object, such as the earth

ex.en: Because of precession, the North Star will change over thousands of years.
ex.zh: 由於歲差，北極星在數千年後會改變。

root.note: 分點逐年往前移動 → 歲差

senses.en: a very steep side of a cliff or mountain
a very dangerous situation

ex.en: The hikers stopped at the edge of the precipice to take photos.
ex.zh: 健行者在懸崖邊停下來拍照。

root.note: 頭朝前栽下去的地方 → 懸崖

senses.en: a cause of a particular action or event; a trigger
(chemistry) a substance that causes precipitation

ex.en: Stress is often a precipitant of migraine headaches.
ex.zh: 壓力常常是偏頭痛的誘因。

root.note: 使事情一頭栽下去的東西 → 誘因

senses.en: to cause something bad to happen suddenly or sooner than expected
[prɪˋsɪpətɪt] done suddenly and without careful thought
(chemistry) a solid that separates from a liquid

ex.en: One small mistake could precipitate a financial crisis.
ex.zh: 一個小錯誤就可能引發金融危機。

root.note: 頭朝前栽下去 → 倉促、突然促成

senses.en: exact and accurate in every detail

ex.en: The recipe gives precise measurements for every ingredient.
ex.zh: 這份食譜每種材料都有精確的份量。

root.note: 把前端切齊 → 精確的

senses.en: the quality of being exact and accurate

ex.en: The surgeon worked with great precision.
ex.zh: 外科醫生以極高的精準度動手術。

root.note: 切得整整齊齊 → 精確

senses.en: to prevent something from happening; to make impossible

ex.en: A busy schedule will preclude me from joining the trip.
ex.zh: 忙碌的行程讓我無法參加這趟旅行。

root.note: 事先把門關上 → 阻止

senses.en: (of a child) having developed certain abilities earlier than usual

ex.en: The precocious six-year-old was already reading novels.
ex.zh: 那個早慧的六歲孩子已經在讀小說了。

root.note: 提早煮熟 → 早熟的

senses.en: a person or thing that comes before and leads to another

ex.en: The abacus was a precursor of the modern calculator.
ex.zh: 算盤是現代計算機的前身。

root.note: 跑在前面的 → 先驅

senses.en: (of an animal) living by killing and eating other animals
seeking to exploit or harm others for gain

ex.en: Sharks are predatory fish found in oceans around the world.
ex.zh: 鯊魚是分布在世界各大洋的掠食性魚類。

root.note: 掠奪的 → 掠食性的

senses.en: a person who held a job or position before someone else
a thing that has been replaced by something newer

ex.en: The new principal promised to continue her predecessor's reforms.
ex.zh: 新校長承諾延續前任校長的改革。

root.note: 之前已離開的人 → 前任

senses.en: a difficult, unpleasant, or embarrassing situation

ex.en: Locked out of the house without a phone, she was in quite a predicament.
ex.zh: 她沒帶手機又被鎖在門外，處境相當尷尬。

root.note: 原指被斷言的狀態、類別 → 引申為處境、困境

senses.en: (grammar) the part of a sentence that says something about the subject
[ˋprɛdɪˏket] to base something on a belief or condition

ex.en: In "The dog barked loudly," the predicate is "barked loudly."
ex.zh: 在 The dog barked loudly 這句裡，述語是 barked loudly。

root.note: 公開說出來、斷定 → 述語

mn: 常見片語 be predicated on：以…為前提。

senses.en: to say that something will happen in the future

ex.en: Experts predict that prices will rise next year.
ex.zh: 專家預測明年物價會上漲。

root.note: 事先說出 → 預測

senses.en: a statement about what will happen in the future

ex.en: His prediction about the election turned out to be correct.
ex.zh: 他對選舉的預測後來證明是對的。

root.note: 事先說出的話 → 預測

senses.en: the state of being greater in number, power, or importance

ex.en: The predominance of young people in the audience surprised the band.
ex.zh: 觀眾以年輕人居多，讓樂團感到意外。

root.note: 統治地位在前 → 優勢

senses.en: present as the strongest or main element

ex.en: Blue is the predominant color in the painting.
ex.zh: 藍色是這幅畫的主色。

root.note: 居於統治地位的 → 主要的

senses.en: to be the strongest or main element; to be greater in number

ex.en: In this forest, pine trees predominate.
ex.zh: 這片森林以松樹居多。

root.note: 處於統治地位 → 佔優勢

senses.en: the fact of being better or more important than all others

ex.en: The university's preeminence in engineering attracts students worldwide.
ex.zh: 這所大學在工程領域首屈一指，吸引了全球學生。

root.note: 突出在所有人前面 → 卓越

senses.en: to take action to prevent something expected from happening
to take or acquire something before others can

ex.en: The company lowered its prices to preempt competition from new rivals.
ex.zh: 公司降價以先發制人，防範新對手的競爭。

root.note: 搶先買下 → 先發制人

senses.en: the act of acting first to prevent something
the right to buy something before others

ex.en: The general argued that preemption was the only way to avoid a larger war.
ex.zh: 那位將軍主張先發制人是避免更大戰爭的唯一方法。

root.note: 搶先取得 → 先發制人、優先購買權

senses.en: to engage, book, or commit in advance

ex.en: We had to preengage the hall months before the wedding.
ex.zh: 我們必須在婚禮前幾個月就預訂禮堂。

root.note: 事先約定

senses.en: to set up or decide in advance

ex.en: It helps to preestablish clear rules before the game starts.
ex.zh: 在比賽開始前預先訂好明確的規則會很有幫助。

root.note: 事先建立

senses.en: to exist at an earlier time or before something else

ex.en: Some of these problems seem to preexist the new policy.
ex.zh: 這些問題有些似乎在新政策之前就已存在。

root.note: 之前就存在

senses.en: existence before something else, especially of the soul before birth
senses.zh: 先存在；（靈魂的）前世存在

ex.en: Some ancient philosophers believed in the preexistence of the soul.
ex.zh: 有些古代哲學家相信靈魂在出生前就已存在。

root.note: 之前就存在

senses.en: an introduction to a book written by the author
to introduce or begin with something

ex.en: In the preface, the author thanks her family for their support.
ex.zh: 作者在序言中感謝家人的支持。

root.note: 在前面說的話 → 序言

senses.en: serving as an introduction

ex.en: After a few prefatory remarks, the speaker got to the main topic.
ex.zh: 講者說了幾句開場白後，進入了主題。

root.note: 在前面說的 → 序言的

senses.en: to like one thing more than another

ex.en: I prefer tea to coffee in the morning.
ex.zh: 早上我比較喜歡喝茶而不是咖啡。

root.note: 把喜歡的放在前面 → 比較喜歡

senses.en: more desirable or suitable

ex.en: Walking is preferable to driving for such a short distance.
ex.zh: 這麼短的距離，走路比開車更好。

root.note: 值得比較喜歡的 → 更好的

senses.en: a greater liking for one thing over another
favor or advantage shown to someone

ex.en: Do you have a preference for a window or an aisle seat?
ex.zh: 你偏好靠窗還是靠走道的座位？

root.note: 比較喜歡的傾向 → 偏好

senses.en: giving an advantage or special treatment to someone
senses.zh: 優惠的；優先的；差別待遇的

ex.en: Members receive preferential treatment when booking tickets.
ex.zh: 會員訂票時可以享有優先待遇。

root.note: 給予優待的

senses.en: promotion to a higher position or office

ex.en: The young officer hoped for preferment after the successful campaign.
ex.zh: 那位年輕軍官希望在戰役成功後獲得晉升。

root.note: 被推舉到前面 → 升遷

senses.en: a group of letters added to the beginning of a word to change its meaning
to add something at the beginning

ex.en: The prefix "un-" turns "happy" into "unhappy."
ex.zh: 字首 un- 把 happy 變成 unhappy。

root.note: 固定在前面的部分 → 字首

senses.en: able to be grasped or seized

ex.en: The handle was shaped to be easily prehensible for small hands.
ex.zh: 這個把手的形狀讓小手也很容易握住。

root.note: 可以抓住的

senses.en: (of a tail or limb) able to grasp or hold things

ex.en: The monkey hung from the branch by its prehensile tail.
ex.zh: 猴子用牠能抓握的尾巴掛在樹枝上。

root.note: 能抓住東西的

senses.en: the action of grasping or seizing
understanding; mental grasp

ex.en: Human hands are highly adapted for prehension.
ex.zh: 人類的手高度適合抓握。

root.note: 抓住的動作（comprehension 同源）

senses.en: an unfair opinion formed without knowledge or reason
to cause someone to have an unfair opinion; to harm

ex.en: The law aims to protect people from prejudice at work.
ex.zh: 這項法律旨在保護人們在職場上免受偏見。

root.note: 事先下判斷 → 偏見

senses.en: the office or rank of a prelate; church government by bishops
senses.zh: 高級教士職位；主教制度

ex.en: The reformers wanted to abolish prelacy and let congregations govern themselves.
ex.zh: 改革者想廢除主教制度，讓各教會自治。

root.note: 高級教士的職位或制度

senses.en: a high-ranking member of the clergy, such as a bishop

ex.en: The prelate led the ceremony in the great cathedral.
ex.zh: 那位高級教士在大教堂主持儀式。

root.note: 被擺在別人前面的人 → 高級教士

senses.en: an action or event that comes before and introduces something more important
a short introductory piece of music

ex.en: The small protests were a prelude to a much larger movement.
ex.zh: 那些小型抗議是一場更大規模運動的序幕。

root.note: 在前面演奏的 → 前奏

senses.en: happening or done before the proper or usual time

ex.en: It is premature to celebrate before all the votes are counted.
ex.zh: 還沒開完票就慶祝還太早。

root.note: 成熟之前 → 過早的

senses.en: a prime minister or head of government
first in importance or quality

ex.en: The premier met with foreign leaders at the summit.
ex.zh: 總理在高峰會上與各國領袖會面。

root.note: 排第一的人 → 首相

mn: premiere（首映）和 premier（首相、首要的）拼法差一個 e。

senses.en: a statement or idea on which an argument or theory is based
(premises) a building and the land around it

ex.en: The whole plan rests on the premise that customers will pay more.
ex.zh: 整個計畫建立在顧客會願意付更多錢的前提上。

root.note: 先放在前面的話 → 前提

senses.en: a strong feeling that something, usually bad, is about to happen

ex.en: She had a premonition that the flight would be delayed.
ex.zh: 她預感班機會延誤。

root.note: 事先的警告 → 預感

senses.en: the state of being completely absorbed in thinking about something
senses.zh: 全神貫注；心事；最關心的事

ex.en: His preoccupation with his phone annoyed everyone at dinner.
ex.zh: 他在晚餐時一直盯著手機，讓大家很不耐煩。

root.note: 心思被事先佔滿 → 全神貫注

senses.en: to fill someone's mind so that they think of little else

ex.en: Try not to let small worries preoccupy you before the exam.
ex.zh: 考試前別讓小事佔據你的心思。

root.note: 事先佔據心思 → 使全神貫注

senses.en: to decide or determine beforehand, as if by fate

ex.en: She did not believe that fate could preordain every event in life.
ex.zh: 她不相信命運能預先決定人生中的每一件事。

root.note: 事先規定好 → 注定

senses.en: the action of making ready for something
a substance prepared for use, such as a medicine

ex.en: Good preparation is the key to doing well on the SAT.
ex.zh: 充分準備是在 SAT 考好的關鍵。

root.note: 事先準備

senses.en: done in order to prepare for something

ex.en: The team held a preparatory meeting before the big presentation.
ex.zh: 團隊在重要簡報前開了一場籌備會議。

root.note: 準備用的

mn: 美國的 prep school 就是 preparatory school（大學預科私校）。

senses.en: greater in number, weight, or importance

ex.en: Tourism is the preponderant source of income on the island.
ex.zh: 觀光業是這座島主要的收入來源。

root.note: 秤起來比較重 → 佔優勢的

senses.en: to be greater in number, weight, or influence

ex.en: In this debate, the arguments for change seem to preponderate.
ex.zh: 在這場辯論中，支持改變的論點似乎佔了上風。

root.note: 重量較重 → 佔優勢

senses.en: an opinion formed beforehand; a bias

ex.en: A fair judge must set aside every prepossession about the case.
ex.zh: 公正的法官必須拋開對案件的一切先入之見。

root.note: 心思被事先佔有 → 成見

senses.en: completely absurd or ridiculous

ex.en: The idea that the moon is made of cheese is preposterous.
ex.zh: 月亮是起司做的這種想法太荒謬了。

root.note: 把後面的放到前面、前後顛倒 → 荒謬的

senses.en: a right or privilege belonging to a particular person or group

ex.en: It is the teacher's prerogative to change the due date.
ex.zh: 更改截止日期是老師的權利。

root.note: 先被徵詢意見的權利 → 特權

senses.en: a sign or warning of a future event
[prɪˋsedʒ] to be a sign that something will happen

ex.en: The early flowers were a presage of a warm spring.
ex.zh: 提早開的花是溫暖春天的預兆。

root.note: 事先察覺 → 預兆

senses.en: knowledge of events before they happen; foresight

ex.en: With remarkable prescience, the writer described smartphones decades early.
ex.zh: 那位作家有驚人的先見之明，早在幾十年前就描寫出智慧型手機。

root.note: 事先知道 → 先見之明

senses.en: having knowledge of events before they happen

ex.en: Her prescient warning about the housing bubble was ignored.
ex.zh: 她對房市泡沫具先見之明的警告被忽視了。

root.note: 事先知道的 → 有先見之明的

senses.en: a rule, law, or command

ex.en: The monks followed every prescript of their ancient order.
ex.zh: 僧侶們遵守他們古老修會的每一條規定。

root.note: 事先寫下的規定

senses.en: (law) subject to or acquired by long-term use or possession
senses.zh: （法律）可依時效取得的；受時效約束的

ex.en: The lawyer argued that the right of way was prescriptible after twenty years of use.
ex.zh: 律師主張，這條通行權在使用二十年後可依時效取得。

root.note: 可依時效規定取得的

senses.en: a doctor's written order for medicine
a recommended way of doing something

ex.en: You need a prescription to buy this medicine.
ex.zh: 買這種藥需要處方。

root.note: 事先寫好的指示 → 處方

senses.en: having a feeling of what is about to happen

ex.en: The old sailor seemed presentient of the storm before any clouds appeared.
ex.zh: 那位老水手似乎在雲還沒出現前就預感到暴風雨要來。

root.note: 事先感覺到的 → 有預感的

senses.en: a feeling that something, especially bad, is about to happen

ex.en: She had a presentiment of danger as she entered the dark alley.
ex.zh: 她走進那條暗巷時，有種危險的預感。

root.note: 事先的感覺 → 預感

senses.en: a formal statement or report, especially one made by a grand jury
the act of presenting something

ex.en: The grand jury issued a presentment criticizing the prison conditions.
ex.zh: 大陪審團發出一份報告，批評監獄的狀況。

root.note: 正式呈上的東西 → 報告

senses.en: the act of keeping something in its original state or safe from harm

ex.en: The group works for the preservation of historic buildings.
ex.zh: 這個團體致力於保存歷史建築。

root.note: 事先保存起來 → 保存

senses.en: an idea taken to be true without proof
behavior that is too bold or disrespectful

ex.en: The law is based on the presumption of innocence until proven guilty.
ex.zh: 這項法律建立在未經證明有罪前推定無罪的原則上。

root.note: 事先就拿來當真 → 假定；擅自拿取 → 放肆

senses.en: failing to respect limits; too bold or confident
senses.zh: 放肆的；冒昧的；自以為是的

ex.en: It would be presumptuous to plan the party before she agrees to come.
ex.zh: 在她答應要來之前就計畫派對，未免太自以為是。

root.note: 不經同意就先拿 → 放肆的

senses.en: a claim or wish to be something, often without justification
the act of pretending to be more important than one is

ex.en: The restaurant serves good food without any pretension.
ex.zh: 這家餐廳的菜很好吃，一點也不做作。

root.note: 把自己伸展到別人面前 → 自命不凡

senses.en: trying to seem more important, intelligent, or cultured than one is

ex.en: He used pretentious words just to impress his classmates.
ex.zh: 他用一些故作高深的字眼，只為了讓同學佩服。

root.note: 把自己撐大給人看 → 做作的

senses.en: beyond what is normal or natural

ex.en: The young pianist showed a preternatural talent for music.
ex.zh: 那位年輕鋼琴家展現出異於常人的音樂天分。

root.note: 超越自然的 → 異常的

senses.en: a false reason given to hide the real reason for an action

ex.en: He called her on the pretext of asking about homework.
ex.zh: 他以問作業為藉口打電話給她。

root.note: 在前面編織的東西 → 藉口

senses.en: the fact of being widespread or common

ex.en: Doctors are studying the prevalence of allergies among children.
ex.zh: 醫生正在研究兒童過敏的普遍程度。

root.note: 力量居前、佔上風 → 盛行

senses.en: widespread in a particular area or time

ex.en: This disease is more prevalent in tropical countries.
ex.zh: 這種疾病在熱帶國家較為普遍。

root.note: 力量居上 → 盛行的

senses.en: to speak evasively or avoid telling the whole truth

ex.en: When asked about the missing money, the treasurer began to prevaricate.
ex.zh: 被問到那筆不見的錢時，財務開始支吾其詞。

parts.m: straddle, walk crookedly 跨開、歪著走

root.note: 走路歪來歪去、不走直路 → 支吾搪塞

senses.en: the act of stopping something from happening

ex.en: Prevention is better than cure.
ex.zh: 預防勝於治療。

root.note: 先到一步擋住 → 預防

senses.en: a small sharp point on a plant or animal
to feel a slight stinging sensation

ex.en: I felt a prickle of fear on the back of my neck.
ex.zh: 我感到後頸一陣發麻的恐懼。

root.note: 小刺

senses.en: self-righteously correct in behavior; smugly moral
senses.zh: 自命清高的；一本正經的

ex.en: His priggish comments about everyone's manners made him unpopular.
ex.zh: 他對大家的禮貌指指點點，自命清高的態度讓他不受歡迎。

root.note: 像道學先生的 → 自命清高的

senses.en: stiffly formal and proper; easily shocked by anything rude
neat and tidy

ex.en: She sat in a prim posture with her hands folded in her lap.
ex.zh: 她拘謹地坐著，雙手交疊放在腿上。

mn: 常見片語 prim and proper：規規矩矩、一板一眼。

senses.en: the chief female singer in an opera
a very temperamental, self-important person

ex.en: The star player acted like a prima donna and refused to practice with the team.
ex.zh: 那位明星球員耍大牌，拒絕和球隊一起練習。

root.note: 第一女士 → 歌劇女主角 → 耍大牌的人

senses.en: an elementary textbook or introduction to a subject

senses.en: of the earliest ages of the world; very ancient

ex.zh: 我們走過一片從未被砍伐過的原始森林。

senses.en: relating to an early stage of development
very simple and basic

ex.zh: 早期人類用石頭製作原始的工具。

senses.en: most important; main
the head of a school

ex.zh: 延誤的主要原因是天氣不好。

senses.en: a state ruled by a prince

senses.en: a basic truth, rule, or belief
a moral rule that guides behavior

senses.en: in its original condition; unspoiled

root.note: 維持原本樣子的 → 原始的

senses.en: a special right or advantage given to a particular person or group

senses.en: (law) a legally recognized relationship between parties, as in a contract
private or secret knowledge shared with others

senses.zh: 知道內情的；參與祕密的

senses.en: the official process of proving that a will is valid

senses.en: a period of supervision given to an offender instead of prison
